uncited: SLAM and Tracking in the context of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) refers to the simultaneous estimation of camera poses and the optimization of the Gaussian scene representation from a stream of images or video.
It solves the problem of building a consistent, real-time 3D model while tracking the camera's trajectory in dynamic or static environments.

What sets this family apart from standard offline 3DGS reconstruction is the online, incremental nature of the optimization, requiring efficient keyframe management, robust tracking against dynamic objects, and real-time rendering feedback for pose correction.
The core mechanism involves coupling a visual odometry or SLAM backend with the differentiable rasterization of 3D Gaussians.

Unlike traditional SLAM systems that rely on sparse feature points or dense depth maps for pose estimation, Gaussian SLAM uses the rendered image or depth from the Gaussian representation as the primary observation model.
**Differentiable Rendering as Observation Model**: The system renders a predicted image $I_{pred}$ from the current camera pose $P$ and Gaussian set $\mathcal{G}$.
The error between $I_{pred}$ and the observed image $I_{obs}$ drives the optimization.
**Joint Optimization**: Camera poses and Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, color) are optimized jointly or alternately.
**Incremental Mapping**: New Gaussians are inserted to cover unobserved or poorly reconstructed regions, and existing Gaussians are pruned or densified based on visibility and error metrics.
**Keyframe Management**: To avoid the computational cost of optimizing all historical data, a sliding window of keyframes is maintained.
